# Object Init

::: {.callout-note appearance="default" collapse="false"}
**Q:** What's the difference between: "object initializer" vs "constructor" vs "constructor body"
:::

Let's dive into your question about object initialization patterns.


## Overview


These are three different ways to set up object state in C#. Let me break them down:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Object Creation Timeline                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                               │
│  1. Constructor Parameters  →  Values passed in              │
│           ↓                                                   │
│  2. Constructor Body       →  Initialization logic runs      │
│           ↓                                                   │
│  3. Object Initializer     →  Properties set after creation  │
│           ↓                                                   │
│  4. Object Ready           →  Fully initialized              │
│                                                               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```


## 1. Constructor


A special method that runs when you create an object. It has **parameters** to receive values.

```csharp
public class Patient
{
    public string HN { get; set; }
    public string Name { get; set; }
    
    // Constructor with parameters
    public Patient(string hn, string name)
    {
        HN = hn;
        Name = name;
    }
}

// Usage
var patient = new Patient("123456", "John Doe");
```

**Python equivalent:**
```python
def __init__(self, hn, name):
    self.hn = hn
    self.name = name
```


## 2. Constructor Body


The **code inside** the constructor that runs during object creation. This is where you write initialization logic.

```csharp
public class DicomStudy
{
    public string StudyInstanceUID { get; set; }
    public DateTime StudyDate { get; set; }
    public string Status { get; set; }
    
    public DicomStudy(string studyUID)
    {
        // ← This whole block is the "constructor body"
        StudyInstanceUID = studyUID;
        StudyDate = DateTime.Now;
        Status = "Pending";
        
        // You can add validation
        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(studyUID))
            throw new ArgumentException("Study UID cannot be empty");
            
        // You can add complex logic
        Console.WriteLine($"Created study: {studyUID}");
    }
}
```


## 3. Object Initializer


Syntax that lets you set **public properties** after the object is created, but in the same statement.

```csharp
public class Modality
{
    public string Code { get; set; }
    public string Description { get; set; }
    public int MaxStudiesPerDay { get; set; }
}

// Object initializer syntax (no constructor needed)
var ct = new Modality
{
    Code = "CT",
    Description = "Computed Tomography",
    MaxStudiesPerDay = 50
};
```


## Complete Comparison Example


```csharp
public class RadiologyReport
{
    public string AccessionNumber { get; set; }
    public string Modality { get; set; }
    public string Status { get; set; }
    public DateTime CreatedDate { get; set; }
    
    // Constructor
    public RadiologyReport(string accessionNumber)
    {
        // Constructor body starts here
        AccessionNumber = accessionNumber;
        CreatedDate = DateTime.Now;
        Status = "Draft"; // Default value
        
        Console.WriteLine("Constructor executed");
        // Constructor body ends here
    }
}

// Method 1: Using constructor only
var report1 = new RadiologyReport("ACC001");
report1.Modality = "CT";

// Method 2: Constructor + Object Initializer
var report2 = new RadiologyReport("ACC002")
{
    // Object initializer - runs AFTER constructor
    Modality = "MRI",
    Status = "Final"  // This overwrites the "Draft" from constructor
};
```


## Execution Order Diagram


```
new RadiologyReport("ACC002") { Modality = "MRI", Status = "Final" }
│
├─ Step 1: Allocate memory for object
│
├─ Step 2: Run Constructor
│   │
│   ├─ AccessionNumber = "ACC002"  (from parameter)
│   ├─ CreatedDate = DateTime.Now  (in constructor body)
│   └─ Status = "Draft"             (in constructor body)
│
├─ Step 3: Run Object Initializer
│   │
│   ├─ Modality = "MRI"             (from initializer)
│   └─ Status = "Final"             (from initializer, OVERWRITES "Draft")
│
└─ Step 4: Return fully initialized object
```


## When to Use Each


**Use Constructor when:**
- Values are **required** for object to be valid
- You need **validation logic**
- You need **complex initialization** (calculations, method calls)
- Setting **read-only** properties (with `{ get; }`)

**Use Object Initializer when:**
- Properties are **optional**
- Simple property assignments
- Want **flexibility** in what to set
- Working with DTOs or POCOs


## Practical Example: DICOM Series


```csharp
public class DicomSeries
{
    public string SeriesInstanceUID { get; }  // Read-only, must use constructor
    public string SeriesDescription { get; set; }
    public string Modality { get; set; }
    public int ImageCount { get; set; }
    public DateTime CreatedDate { get; }
    
    // Constructor for required fields
    public DicomSeries(string seriesUID, string modality)
    {
        // Constructor body - validation and required fields
        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(seriesUID))
            throw new ArgumentException("Series UID required");
            
        SeriesInstanceUID = seriesUID;  // Must set here (read-only)
        Modality = modality;
        CreatedDate = DateTime.Now;
        ImageCount = 0;  // Default
    }
}

// Usage: Constructor + Object Initializer together
var series = new DicomSeries("1.2.840.113...", "CT")
{
    SeriesDescription = "Chest CT with contrast",
    ImageCount = 150
};
```


## Comparison to Other Languages


**Dart/Flutter:**
```dart
class Patient {
  String hn;
  String name;
  
  // Constructor
  Patient(this.hn, this.name);  // Short syntax
  
  // Named parameters (similar to object initializer)
  Patient.withName({required this.hn, required this.name});
}
```

**Python:**
```python
# Constructor
class Patient:
    def __init__(self, hn, name):  # Constructor body
        self.hn = hn
        self.name = name

# Python doesn't have object initializer syntax
# But you can use dict unpacking
patient = Patient(**{'hn': '123', 'name': 'John'})
```


## Key Takeaways


```
┌──────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  │ When It Runs                            │
├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Constructor      │ When 'new' keyword is used              │
│ Constructor Body │ The code inside constructor             │
│ Object Init.     │ AFTER constructor, before assignment    │
└──────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
